Senior Manager, Supply Chain (Robot Production)
Genesis
San Carlos , California 
About Genesis
We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.
We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.
The role
Every part that goes into our robot: who makes it, at what price, on what lead time, to what quality. This is the hands-on role. You build the supplier base for production, develop domestic sources for the sub-systems that need them, and make sure the line never waits on a part. You start with a bill of materials, a design team and a few suppliers; you end with a qualified, dual-sourced supply chain that supports production with our manufacturing partner. You are at our facility, at the partner and at suppliers more than you are at a desk.
What you'll do
Be on the floor: at our facility, at our manufacturing partner and at suppliers; first articles, line-down calls and recoveries are yours.
Build the supplier base: source, qualify and manage suppliers for machined and cast structures, gears and actuators, motors, PCBAs, harnesses, shells, batteries and sensors; two sources for every critical sub-system.
Develop domestic suppliers for the sub-systems that need them, and keep the content records that come with selling into regulated markets.
Run the commercial work day to day: RFQs, should-cost, piece price and tooling negotiation, payment and warranty terms; work with Legal on supplier agreements.
Sit in design reviews from the start: flag long-lead, single-source and high-risk parts before design freeze; bring supplier capability into the design.
Own clear-to-build and the plan: every unit on the schedule has a complete kit before it starts; a rolling plan the line, the partner and the suppliers all see; capacity planning with suppliers ahead of demand; inventory accuracy and safety stock by part class.
Own the BOM in production: cost roll-ups by phase, engineering change control with the design team and Manufacturing Engineering, cost-down from pilot to volume.
Build the supplier quality loop with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality: first article and PPAP where it applies, incoming inspection, supplier scorecards and quarterly reviews, corrective action and recovery.
Run logistics: inbound, between our facility and our partner's, import and export paperwork with Legal, spares and service parts.
Run the systems we have and help stand up the next ones: part numbering, BOM control, MRP; own the weekly numbers (clear-to-build, on-time delivery, PPV, inventory).
What we are looking for
You have built a supplier base for a hardware product going into production, not managed or handed to you, and you produce results in weeks, not quarters.
Deep experience with machined and cast metal parts, gears or actuators, motors, PCBAs and harnesses, and the suppliers who make them; you read drawings and GD&T.
You have developed new suppliers in new regions and qualified them to a standard.
Strong commercial record: you have negotiated price, tooling and terms with suppliers and contract manufacturers.
You are fluent in BOMs, change control, should-cost and cost roll-ups, and comfortable with the people who design the product.
8 or more years in supply chain, sourcing or supplier development for complex hardware, with time in a mature organization so you know what the systems look like at scale; you have led a small team or are ready to; engineering degree preferred.
Bonus: robotics or automotive; contract manufacturer selection and transition; import and export compliance; APICS or CPSM.
Working Conditions
Office and production environments; travel to suppliers and partner sites, including international, up to 30%.
How we work
We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:
Limitless ambition.
We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.
Relentless urgency.
Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.
Type-2 Fun.
Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.
Radical transparency.
Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.
Multiculturalism
. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.
Team over ego.
Help others, share context, and win as a team.
A joyful journey.
We take pride in the craft, enjoy the ride, and make space to laugh. Happiness is part of how we get there.

Multi-Site Manufacturing Leader
DuPont Water Solutions is seeking a passionate and high-performing individual to lead our reverse osmosis (RO) and ultrafiltration (UF) manufacturing network. The Multi-Site Manufacturing Leader is responsible for leading a global portfolio of (7) manufacturing sites and driving safe, reliable, customer-focused, and cost-effective operations aligned to DuPont’s business strategy. This role provides enterprise manufacturing leadership across a diverse network of sites, partnering closely with business, commercial, supply chain, engineering, quality, EHS, technology, and operational excellence leaders to align manufacturing priorities with customer needs, deliver performance, build capability, maximize value, and enable growth.
This individual will be accountable for establishing and sustaining a lean manufacturing culture that improves every day, reduces waste and variation, strengthens daily management, and develops problem-solving capability at all levels of the organization. Success requires a visible, hands-on leader who can set strategy, drive disciplined execution, inspire global teams, and role model DuPont’s core values of Safety & Respect, Integrity & Accountability, Grow and Improve, and Solve Problems with Customers.

Lead global manufacturing performance: Own performance across the portfolio of RO and UF manufacturing sites, delivering results in safety, quality, delivery, inventory, productivity (cost), compliance, asset reliability, and customer service.
Drive lean manufacturing and operational excellence: Establish and deploy lean manufacturing practices, daily management systems, standard work, visual management, value stream mapping, kaizen, structured problem solving, root cause analysis, and waste elimination across the manufacturing network.
Align manufacturing strategy to business priorities: Develop and execute integrated manufacturing plans that support growth, margin improvement, customer commitments, supply reliability, and long-term competitiveness.
Sponsor and ensure progress of priority projects and investments: Develop priorities for capital investments based on economic models and ensure proper resource allocation to support realization of business strategy. Partner with capital organization and manufacturing technology on developing optionality and strong basic data with cross functional review in support of capital allocation process.
Improve customer experience through end-to-end excellence: Partners closely with commercial, customer service, procurement, logistics and supply chain to ensure end-to-end processes supporting customer expectations around lead time and excellent delivery performance. Sponsor efforts to streamline processes and drive improvements across the order-to-cash process.

Build a culture of continuous improvement: Create an environment where leaders and teams challenge the status quo, solve problems at the source in real-time, learn from failures, and continuously improve processes, performance, and ways of working.
Lead through metrics and operating cadence: Use KPIs, bowler metrics, tiered accountability, operating reviews, and data-driven insights to identify performance gaps, prioritize improvement opportunities, develop action plans, execute Kaizens and sustain results.
Develop manufacturing talent and capability: Attract, develop, coach, and retain strong manufacturing leaders and technical talent; build lean capability, succession depth, and engaged shop-floor teams across regions.
Strengthen manufacturing systems and standards: Partner with Operational Excellence, Engineering, Quality, EHS, Supply Chain, and IT/OT teams to standardize best practices, codify tools and processes, and accelerate adoption of scalable manufacturing systems.
Lead change across a global network: Influence and align stakeholders across businesses, regions, functions, and sites. Improve cost, productivity, and asset effectiveness: Drive productivity, yield improvement (reduce cost of poor quality), cycle-time reduction, scrap and waste elimination, energy efficiency, and asset utilization while maintaining strong safety, quality, and compliance standards.
Role model DuPont culture and values: Set the tone through consistent behaviors, decision-making, and communications that reinforce safety, respect, integrity, accountability, continuous improvement, and customer-focused problem solving.

Execution-focused: Translates strategy into clear priorities, operating rhythms, accountability, and measurable results; drives issues to closure with urgency and discipline.

Visible and people-centered: Builds trust on the shop floor, engages teams directly, listens actively, and creates an environment where people are empowered to identify and solve problems.

Vice President of Operations
Genesis Products
Goshen, IN
Genesis Products is looking for a VP of Operations to take a strong manufacturing foundation and turn it into a competitive weapon. This is a new, company-wide role created for one reason: our customers move fast, our business is getting more complex, and we want manufacturing systems smart enough to make complexity an advantage.
You won't inherit a mess to clean up. You'll inherit working systems, monthly audits, committed plant teams, and leaders who want to get better. Launches and overhauls.

Warehouse and material excellence.

Logistics.
Lead our logistics function and managed fleet, and expand it beyond Elkhart into a true competitive advantage.
What success looks like in your first two years
Safety and audit results are improving across every plant, and leadership reviews system health as seriously as revenue and margin.
Our existing systems are stronger than when you arrived, and no plant has slipped backward.
Underperforming operations have been turned around with results that last.
Plants respond to customer changes faster, with less disruption and lower cost.

A track record of turnarounds, launches, or integrations, with results you can measure and that lasted after you moved on.

How you work:
You build on what's there.
You learn why existing systems work before changing them, and you improve them instead of replacing them to leave your mark.
You lead through influence.

The customer comes first, and you're comfortable when daily decisions go to the business. But you'll speak up, to anyone, when a shortcut is turning into a habit.

We're hiring a Vice President of Engineering, R&D to build SerenX's engineering headquarters in Melbourne, Florida.

The pace we are building for is chalkboard to first operational employment in months, not years, when the hardware, the law, and the end user allow it.
You may have spent years on flight hardware at a place like SpaceX, Blue Origin, L3Harris, or Northrop Grumman. You learned how ambitious hardware gets built, and you learned how a large organization can make that work harder than it needs to be. You want to build something of your own.
The Founder and CTO sets the technology. You lead the people, the execution, and the engineering organization that turn that direction into working, fielded systems. Hire for ability, integrity, curiosity, and how someone treats the people beside them.
Give every engineer clear ownership, and a path to get better that does not require them to become a manager.

Evidence you have led, or are ready to lead, on the order of 15 to 50 people, and that you can name the leads who made that possible.

A record of recruiting and growing engineers who would work for you again.
You can move fast and still stop a test, a design, or a date when the evidence says to.
Willingness to work on-site in Melbourne, Florida and be on the range with the team.
A bachelor's degree in engineering, physics, or a related field, or equivalent depth of engineering and leadership experience.

A director or senior director ready to leave SpaceX, Blue Origin, L3Harris, Northrop Grumman, Collins, Lockheed Martin, Rocket Lab, Anduril, or a smaller shop that actually flies hardware, and build the organization you wish you had worked in.
You have already been the person between a founder, or a chief engineer, and a team.
You have grown a team from a small founding group toward a larger multidisciplinary shop, and developed the leads as you went.
Missiles, interceptors, UAVs, spacecraft, propulsion, or flight test.
Configuration, test readiness, and production discipline put in place without freezing a young program.
Experience with DoD customers, export-controlled technology, or military operational requirements.

You have reached the point where building great engineers matters as much to you as building great machines. You remember what it was like to be young, with an ambitious idea, and to have someone senior who believed in you. You want to be that person for someone else.

We care more about the people you have developed, and the hardware you helped deliver, than the number of people who reported to you.

Chief Operating Officer (COO)
Multi-Site Manufacturing, Supply Chain & Distribution
Position Overview
We are seeking a hands-on, strategic Chief Operating Officer to lead end-to-end operations for a growing, private equity-backed manufacturing and distribution business. Reporting to the CEO, the COO will oversee manufacturing, assembly, supply chain, procurement, quality, logistics, and distribution across domestic and international locations.
This executive will translate business strategy into disciplined execution, strengthen operational infrastructure, and build the capabilities needed to support continued growth. The ideal candidate combines strong manufacturing and financial acumen with experience leading both internal operations and international third-party manufacturing partners.
The COO will partner closely with commercial, product development, engineering, and finance leaders to improve profitability, introduce new products, and scale operations while preserving quality, craftsmanship, and an entrepreneurial culture.
Key Responsibilities
Enterprise Strategy & Operational Execution
Develop and execute a multi-year operations strategy aligned with business growth, customer commitments, and financial objectives.
Translate strategic priorities into capacity, manufacturing network, technology, talent, and capital investment plans with clear ownership and milestones.
Establish consistent operating reviews, performance dashboards, and accountability across locations.
Partner with the CEO and CFO on annual budgets, forecasting, long-range planning, and board reporting.
Multi-Site Manufacturing & Operational Excellence
Lead safety, quality, productivity, cost, capacity utilization, and on-time delivery across manufacturing, assembly, and distribution facilities.
Coach and hold facility leaders accountable for measurable performance improvements.
Apply Lean principles, process standardization, automation, and continuous improvement to increase efficiency and scalability.
Evaluate manufacturing footprints and make-versus-buy decisions to balance cost, capacity, quality, and service.
Build consistent operating disciplines while respecting the specialized capabilities and culture of each facility.
Global Supply Chain, Procurement & Distribution
Own strategic sourcing, procurement, supplier performance, inventory management, transportation, fulfillment, and distribution.
Manage international suppliers and contract manufacturing partners, including relationships in Asia.
Strengthen supplier quality, delivery, cost competitiveness, and capacity while reducing supply risk.
Improve material availability, lead times, logistics costs, and working capital.
Oversee domestic and international shipping and coordinate applicable trade and customs requirements.
Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning
Lead a disciplined Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning (SIOP) or integrated business planning process.
Align demand forecasts with production, supplier capacity, inventory, and financial commitments.
Use scenario planning to respond to demand fluctuations, supply constraints, and growth opportunities.
Improve forecast accuracy, customer service, inventory turns, and cash generation.
New Product Introduction & Engineering Partnership
Lead the operational transition of new products from engineering designs into sourcing, manufacturing, assembly, and distribution.
Establish launch processes, stage gates, ownership, and readiness requirements.
Partner with engineering on manufacturability, product cost, supplier readiness, tooling, capacity, and quality.
Deliver successful launches that balance speed-to-market, cost, and reliability while protecting existing production commitments.
Quality, Safety & Compliance
Establish and sustain an effective quality management system across internal facilities and external manufacturing partners.
Lead applicable ISO certification efforts, audit readiness, corrective actions, and continuous improvement.
Strengthen supplier quality controls, process consistency, and product reliability.
Promote a culture of safety and accountability across all locations.
Engage directly with key customers and distributors to address quality concerns and build confidence in operational performance.
Systems, Data & Financial Performance
Develop the operations technology roadmap, including ERP/MRP capabilities, planning tools, dashboards, and process controls.
Improve data accuracy, visibility, and decision-making across facilities.
Partner with finance to improve product costing, gross margins, productivity, inventory, and working capital.
Evaluate capital investments using clear business cases and return-on-investment analysis.
Leadership & Organizational Development
Build, develop, and retain a high-performing team of facility leaders and functional managers.
Clarify organizational responsibilities, decision authority, goals, and performance expectations.
Strengthen succession planning and leadership development.
Foster collaboration across operations, sales, engineering, product development, and finance.
Serve as a trusted operational advisor to the CEO and contribute to board and investor discussions as appropriate.
Qualifications
15+ years of progressive operations leadership experience, including significant responsibility for multi-site manufacturing and supply chain.
Prior experience as a COO, Senior Vice President, Vice President of Operations, or equivalent executive leader.
Experience overseeing both in-house manufacturing or assembly and outsourced production.
Demonstrated experience managing international supply chains and manufacturing partners, including Asia.
Proven success improving productivity, quality, delivery, margins, and working capital in a growing business.
Strong ownership of SIOP or integrated business planning.
Experience leading new product introductions, strategic sourcing, supplier development, and manufacturing process improvements.
Working knowledge of quality management systems, ISO standards, and continuous improvement.
Strong financial acumen, including product cost, gross margin, budgeting, capital allocation, and investment analysis.
Experience using ERP/MRP systems and operational analytics to drive performance.
Demonstrated ability to develop leaders and build accountability across geographically dispersed teams.
Preferred Background
Experience in a private equity-backed, founder-led, or entrepreneurial manufacturing business.
Background in automotive, performance aftermarket, metal fabrication, engineered products, industrial equipment, public safety, defense, or other quality-critical manufacturing environments.
Experience with high-mix production, international operations, acquisitions, or operational integration.
Experience presenting to boards, investors, and executive leadership teams.
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations, supply chain, business, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience considered.
Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or higher, or comparable practical experience, strongly preferred.
Leadership Style
The successful candidate will be an action-oriented executive who moves comfortably between strategic planning and hands-on problem-solving. This leader will earn credibility with executives, facility teams, and skilled trades through sound judgment, clear communication, and consistent follow-through.
A strong sense of urgency, attention to detail, and commitment to people development are essential, along with the ability to introduce structure while preserving the culture and expertise that make the business successful.
Location & Travel
Based at a primary U.S. operating location, with regular travel to domestic facilities, international sites, and manufacturing partners.

About CIRCOR Aerospace & Defense
CIRCOR Aerospace & Defense is focused on the design, development, and manufacture of specialty fluid and motion control products for demanding aerospace and defense applications. CIRCOR products are flying on most commercial and military aircraft, including single and twin aisle air transport, business and regional jets, military transports and fighters, and commercial and military rotorcraft. Other markets include unmanned aircraft, shipboard applications, and military ground vehicles.
Business units are in Corona, California; Warren, Massachusetts; Hauppauge, New York; Paris, France; Uxbridge, UK; and Tangier, Morocco. Parent company CIRCOR International is headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts and CIRCOR Aerospace & Defense is headquartered in Corona, California.
POSITION DETAILS
Position Summary
As the Director of Quality, you will be responsible for leading quality initiatives that directly support our operational and site objectives. You will drive continuous improvement efforts focused on zero defect methodologies that aim to eliminate errors and defects in all production, office, engineering and service stages. The hands-on Quality leader is a leadership team member responsible for leading the organization. As a leadership team member, the successful candidate will partner with other staff members to execute the commitments of the business. Quality leadership includes recruiting, developing, training, coaching, goal and performance management. Shop floor processes producing close tolerance aerospace components produced via built to specification (BTS), build to print (BTP), maintenance repair and overhaul (MRO), supplemental type certification (STC), and Parts Manufacturing Approval (PMA). Responsible for Quality Leadership for a Repair Station. Typical processes include milling, lathe, hone, plating, CNC programming, assembly, testing, non-destructive testing, dimensional and visual inspection techniques, and electro-mechanical processes. Lead customer, in-house, and supplier quality requirements through ISO/AS, NADCAP, FAA, C.A.S.E., ANSI, and other specifications. The hands-on individual will analyze and interpret technical data (engineering drawings, specifications, purchase orders, etc.) and support shop routings, operations sheets, tools, and other necessary processes to produce a high-quality product.

Drive business metrics (safety, quality, on-time delivery, cost)
Zero Defect Plans
Driving systematic reduction of quality issues
Drive Prevention
Drive RCCA
Lead of Quality technical team
Interface with customers on key quality issues and initiatives
Own the QMS
Build and develop a high-performing quality team; provide hands-on coaching, establish performance standards, and foster a culture of accountability and continuous improvement
Lead quality system requirements, Build to Specifications, Build to Print, Repair Station
Lean / six sigma champion

Comply with all company policies/procedures.
Comply with all military and contractual requirements.
Perform additional related duties as assigned.

10 – 15 years of experience
Quality leadership, ability to mentor, coach, develop and build a high functioning quality team.
Quality systems experience, extensive understanding of quality systems and quality engineering focusing on lean manufacturing and lean processes in Build to Specifications, Build to Print, Repair Station, STC and PMA
High ethical standards. Models and supports organization’s goals and values; adapts to changing conditions; demonstrates persistence and overcomes obstacles.
Strong project management skills, including the ability to prioritize, balance, and manage multiple efforts with strong results/goal orientation. Use time effectively, prioritizes and organizes workflow; can orchestrate multiple activities at once. Agility and personal adaptability with the ability to successfully manage multiple priorities with a high sense of urgency in a rapidly changing environment.
Solid analytical skills and solution-driven thinking; collects and researches data; uses intuition and experience to complement data. Make good decisions based upon a mixture of analysis, wisdom, experience and judgment.
Identifies and resolves problems in a timely manner; develops alternative solutions; works well in group problem solving situations; presents ideas and information in a manner that gets others' attention; displays willingness to make decisions; exhibits sound and accurate judgment; supports and explains reasoning for decisions includes appropriate people in decision-making process.

Excellent communication (oral and written) and interpersonal skills with the ability to convey information and ideas in a variety of media, tactful, confident, at all levels, internal and external.
